- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price has recently spiked, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use moving average to smooth.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is trending, model frequently underestimates mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 10–20% if sentiment is weak; if sentiment is strong, retain or slightly increase.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates late-period price (last 7–10 days); apply 1–3% downward adjustment if sentiment is stable or mildly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows sharp reversal (e.g., 0.8 → 0.1), model may lag; forecast should adjust 1–2 days ahead of true trend reversal.
